subject: MSA / Order Form — end-of-term grace, auto-renew opt-out and termination-for-convenience alignment
messages:
From: Susan Lawson <susan.lawson@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, mark.chen@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on termination & auto-renew windows in the redline

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for sending the redline. Our legal and procurement teams have a couple of asks we want to surface before we re-share the document:

- Can Redwood make the auto-renew opt-out window at least 60 days instead of 30? Our fiscal close requires 45+ days notice.
- Relatedly, we want termination for convenience to allow a 90-day transition for any dedicated capacity commitments. Would Redwood be open to a mutual termination-for-convenience clause (customer OR vendor) limited to contract year-end, or do you require customer-only TOC?

We attached the Order Form comments in-line and highlighted the term mechanics. Mark (legal) and procurement on cc — please advise if these are deal blockers or if we can find alternate commercial mitigations.

Thanks,
Susan Lawson
Director, Strategic Procurement
Acme Health, Inc.

Attachment: OrderForm_Acme_v2.pdf (see p.2 term table)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lawson <susan.lawson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on termination & auto-renew windows in the redline

Susan — thanks for the clear asks. High level: we want to be flexible for enterprise procurement cycles but also balance capacity economics for Dedicated pools. A few options we typically offer:

1) Standard: 12-month term, auto-renews for 12 months, 30-day written opt-out prior to renewal (no refunds for partial periods).
2) Procurement-friendly: 12-month term, auto-renew with 60-day opt-out (we require confirmation 60 days before renewal) — customer can choose this in the Order Form; we charge a 10% scheduling premium for Dedicated pools to compensate for reallocation risk.
3) Mutual TOC: mutual termination-for-convenience with 60–90 day notice and pro-rated refund for pre-paid unused months (subject to minimum usage commitment).

If Acme prefers a 90-day mutual TOC and a 60-day opt-out, we can offer that but need legal to confirm the refund mechanics and a scheduling premium on Dedicated. I can loop in Karthik and Legal to draft precise language.

Next step: do you want us to provide redline language for the MSA and Order Form that reflects option 2 or option 3? Happy to prepare both and flag the operational impacts.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: MSA_Redline_Acme_v3.docx

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme — term/renewal asks (we need legal draft + pricing note)

Jonas / Aditya / Karthik — forwarding Acme's note. Quick take from GTM: procurement will push 60–90 day windows; we should avoid a churnable 30-day reset on large Dedicated commitments.

Ask for legal: can we draft both: (A) 60-day opt-out + scheduling premium, and (B) mutual TOC with 90-day notice + pro-rated refund (with minimum fee). For (B) we should explicitly exclude early termination from being used to avoid committed spend for Dedicated GPUs during the notice period (i.e., customer pays through the last day of the notice period).

Aditya — if you can confirm whether we can accept a 10% premium, I'll include that in the commercial proposal.

Lauren
Head of Customer Success (cc for onboarding implications)

Subject: Re: Acme — pricing impact for 60/90-day options

Team — pricing confirms we can accept the 60-day opt-out (option A) with a 10% scheduling premium for Dedicated pools. For the mutual TOC (option B) with 90-day notice and pro-rated refunds, pricing requests a minimum termination fee equal to one month of committed capacity to avoid switching costs.

Proposed commercial bullets to give Acme:
- Option A: 12-month term, auto-renew, 60-day written opt-out before renewal; no refunds; 10% Dedicated scheduling premium.
- Option B: 12-month term, mutual termination-for-convenience (90 days notice); pro-rated refund for unused pre-paid months less a one-month minimum termination fee; Dedicated capacity billed through notice period.

If legal approves the specific clause text (we should limit retroactive backdating language and avoid long-tailed obligations), I can update the Order Form with pricing variants.

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Susan — following up with a single package so procurement and legal can review quickly. Attached is a redline bundle with two tracked options:

- Option A (Procurement-friendly): 60-day auto-renew opt-out; no refunds; 10% scheduling premium for Dedicated capacity.
- Option B (Mutual TOC): Mutual termination-for-convenience with 90-day notice; pro-rated refund for unused pre-paid months less a one-month termination minimum; Dedicated capacity billed through notice period.

I’ve asked Karthik to prepare precise MSA language for Option B around the refund calc, minimum fee, and a clause that prevents termination being used to avoid committed scheduling obligations (we propose a one-month minimum). We also attached an illustrative Order Form with toggles for the two options so procurement can pick.

DocuSign / next steps: if Acme prefers Option A we can finalize commercial terms and send a DocuSign envelope within 48 hours. If you prefer Option B, please confirm and I’ll have Legal circulate the MSA redline for final sign-off — that will add ~5 business days to the timeline.

Link: https://redwood.app/docusign/ACME-3472 (DocuSign envelope placeholder)

Thanks for the collaboration — happy to jump on a short call if Mark or procurement want to walk through the impacts.

Best,
Jonas Weber
